postTitle: Tax-Loss Harvesting and Asset Location Explained
topic: A loss can delay tax on a gain; the delayed tax stays invested, and it is a delay, not a saving

assumptions.notes: Lesson example, illustrative rates: €10,000 gain taxed at 25% = €2,500. €2,500 at 7% a year for 20 years = €9,674, about €9,700. Not the net benefit: the replacement has a lower purchase price, so a later sale may owe more tax.

caption.instagram:
You owe tax on a gain, and another investment is below what you paid. Could that loss delay the tax?

The example: a €10,000 gain taxed at 25% is €2,500 of tax. Where the rules allow, a €10,000 loss sold in the same year cancels the gain, so the €2,500 is not paid now. Left invested at 7% a year, it could reach about €9,700 after 20 years.

That is not the benefit. The replacement was bought at a lower price, so a later sale can owe more tax. What is left depends on future tax rates, the years held and trading costs. Many countries also limit selling at a loss and buying the same thing straight back.
